title: Tokyo · Osaka · Kyoto — 10 Days of Family Adventure: Temples, Tonkotsu & Toddler-Friendly Thrills Across Japan's Golden Route
description: A packed yet toddler-paced journey through Japan's three most iconic cities. Mornings start with matcha, days are filled with shrines, character cafés, and street food, and nights come alive with neon-lit shopping and late-night eats — all without a single bite of pork.

days.title: Touchdown Tokyo — Shibuya After Dark
days.description: Land at Narita ~1pm, grab your pocket WiFi and IC cards, then Narita Express straight to Shibuya. Check into your Airbnb, freshen up, and hit the neon streets for your first taste of Tokyo.

activities.name: Narita Airport → Shibuya
activities.description: Collect bags, buy Suica/Pasmo cards at the JR counter, pick up pocket WiFi. Take the Narita Express (N'EX) to Shibuya Station (~90 min). Kids under 6 ride free.

activities.name: Shibuya Crossing & Hachikō Statue
activities.description: The world's busiest intersection — watch the scramble from the Starbucks above or walk right through it. Find the loyal dog Hachikō statue outside the station. The legendary discount store — everything from snacks to toys to cosplay. Kids will love the candy floor. Tax-free for purchases over ¥5,000.

activities.name: Shibuya Center-Gai & Night Walk
activities.description: Stroll the neon-lit pedestrian streets. Hit up Seria (100-yen shop) for toddler entertainment supplies and Uniqlo Shibuya for any travel gear you forgot.

days.title: Matcha, Meiji & Kawaii Culture
days.description: Start with matcha in the forest, visit Tokyo's grandest shrine, then dive into Harajuku's kaleidoscopic kawaii world. End the day 230m above Shibuya.

activities.name: Meiji Jingū Shrine
activities.description: Walk through the towering torii gate and forested path to Tokyo's most important Shinto shrine. Write wishes on ema wooden plaques. Stroller-friendly main path. Right next to Meiji Shrine — let the toddlers run free on the wide lawns. Weekend performers and food stalls often set up near the entrance.

activities.name: Takeshita Street
activities.description: Tokyo's famous teen fashion corridor — rainbow cotton candy, crepe shops, character goods stores, and wild fashion. Stroller navigable but crowded on weekends. Adorable Miffy-themed café with character-shaped food and drinks. Book ahead — very popular with families.

activities.name: Shibuya Sky Observation Deck
activities.description: 230m above the city on the rooftop of Shibuya Scramble Square. Open-air deck with stunning 360° views. Time it for golden hour → sunset. Book tickets online in advance.

activities.name: Shibuya Character Stores Marathon
activities.description: Shibuya 109 area has Nintendo Store, Pokémon Center, One Piece Store, and more character shops. Perfect evening stroll with the kids.

days.title: Shinjuku — Gardens, Gai & the 3D Cat
days.description: Shinjuku is a universe unto itself. Serene gardens in the morning, the famous 3D cat at noon, shopping and anime stores in the afternoon, and the electric buzz of Golden Gai after dark.

activities.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
activities.description: One of Tokyo's most beautiful parks — Japanese garden, English landscape garden, and greenhouse. Huge lawns perfect for toddlers to explore. No alcohol, no play equipment — just pure nature.

activities.name: 3D Giant Cat — Cross Shinjuku Vision
activities.description: The viral 3D cat billboard on the Shinjuku Alta building. It 'wakes up' and interacts with the crowd on the hour. Toddlers will lose their minds. Vintage anime, manga, games, and retro collectibles. Great for finding One Piece and Naruto treasures at reasonable prices.

activities.name: Kabukichō & Godzilla Head
activities.description: Tokyo's entertainment district — see the giant Godzilla head on the Hotel Gracery rooftop. Walk through the neon canyon of Kabukichō. Themed food hall inside Kabukichō — each stall has wild decor. Find chicken yakitori, seafood, and beef options (no pork section clearly marked).

activities.time: 🌙 Evening — Golden Gai & Late Night Eats
activities.name: Shinjuku Golden Gai
activities.description: 200+ tiny bars in narrow alleys — many seat only 6 people. A few are family-friendly in the early evening (before 9pm). Unique atmosphere you won't find anywhere else.

days.title: Temples, Towers & Sunshine City
days.description: Old-meets-new Tokyo: the ancient Sensō-ji temple in the morning, futuristic Skytree at midday, then Ikebukuro's Sunshine City and Pokémon Center for an anime-filled afternoon.

activities.name: Sensō-ji Temple
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest temple (645 AD). Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate), browse Nakamise-dōri shopping street, and draw your fortune (omikuji). The famous fish market's outer market is still thriving. Fresh seafood, tamagoyaki (egg omelet), and skewered treats. Kid-friendly: tamagoyaki on a stick and fresh fruit.

activities.name: Tokyo Skytree
activities.description: 634m tall — Japan's tallest structure. The Tembo Deck (350m) has floor-to-ceiling windows. Solamachi mall at the base has tons of character shops and a food court.

activities.name: Sunshine City
activities.description: Massive entertainment complex in Ikebukuro — aquarium, planetarium, Namco arcade, and Pokémon Center. You could spend hours here. The flagship Pokémon store — massive selection of plushies, cards, apparel, and exclusives you can't find elsewhere. Located inside Sunshine City.

activities.name: Surugaya Ikebukuro
activities.description: Another vintage anime/manga shop — different stock from the Shinjuku location. Worth a browse for rare finds.

days.title: Art, Cats & the Tower — Tokyo's Greatest Hits
days.description: An unforgettable day: wade through digital art at teamLab Planets, visit the lucky cat temple, stand beneath Tokyo Tower at sunset, and soak at a 24-hour onsen spa.

activities.name: teamLab Planets TOKYO DMM
activities.description: Walk barefoot through immersive digital art installations — water rooms, infinity mirror gardens, and flower universes. Toddlers love it (the shallow water rooms are a huge hit). Book the earliest slot for fewer crowds.

activities.name: Gotokuji Temple (Cat Temple)
activities.description: The birthplace of the maneki-neko (lucky beckoning cat). Thousands of white cat figurines fill the shelves — it's mesmerizing. Buy a small cat to leave as an offering or take home.

activities.name: Hie-jinja Shrine
activities.description: Beautiful hilltop shrine with a dramatic tunnel of red torii gates (mini Fushimi Inari vibes). The senbon torii stairway is stunning but stroller-unfriendly — take the elevator side entrance. The 333m red-and-white icon. Main Deck at 150m has glass floor panels and great views. Lights up beautifully at night but the daytime views are clearer.

activities.name: Toyosu Manyo Club (24-Hour Resort Spa)
activities.description: Hot spring resort near teamLab Planets area. Multiple baths, relaxation rooms, and a restaurant. Kids welcome in family baths. Perfect way to end a big sightseeing day.

days.title: Shinkansen to Osaka — Dōtonbori After Dark
days.description: Last morning in Tokyo for any missed spots, then bullet train to Osaka. Check into your hotel and dive straight into the sensory overload of Dōtonbori.

activities.time: 🍵 Morning — Last Tokyo Stop & Kirby Café
activities.name: Kirby Café TOKYO
activities.description: Nintendo's Kirby-themed café in Tokyo Solamachi (Skytree complex). Adorable character food — Kirby curry, Waddle Dee pancakes, star-shaped desserts. MUST book in advance (opens 1 month prior).

activities.name: Tokyo Station → Shin-Osaka (Shinkansen)
activities.description: Take the Tōkaidō Shinkansen (Nozomi) — 2 hours 30 minutes. Reserve seats (Green Car or regular) for family comfort. Buy ekiben (station bento) for the ride.

activities.name: Check into Osaka Hotel
activities.description: Drop bags, freshen up. If staying near Namba/Shinsaibashi, you're walking distance to everything.

activities.name: Dōtonbori
activities.description: Osaka's most iconic street — giant neon signs, the Glico Running Man, and endless food stalls. The canal is beautiful at night. This is Japan's street food capital.

days.title: Kyoto Day Trip — Thousand Gates & Geisha Streets
days.description: Train from Osaka to Kyoto for a full day of temple magic. Early start at Fushimi Inari to beat crowds, then Gion's geisha district, Nishiki Market for lunch, and matcha everything.

activities.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
activities.description: 10,000 vermillion torii gates snaking up a mountainside — Japan's #1 most-visited shrine. Go EARLY (before 8am) to avoid crowds. You don't need to hike the full 2 hours — the first 20 minutes gives you the iconic tunnel photos.

activities.name: Gion (Geisha District)
activities.description: Kyoto's most atmospheric neighborhood — wooden machiya townhouses, stone-paved streets, and if you're lucky, a glimpse of a maiko (apprentice geisha). Walk down Hanami-koji street. Traditional Kyoto tea house experience — ceremonial matcha and wagashi (traditional sweets). Calm, beautiful, and a real taste of Kyoto culture.

activities.name: Nishiki Market (Kyoto's Kitchen)
activities.description: 400m covered shopping street with 130+ stalls. Fresh seafood, pickles, mochi, matcha sweets, and Kyoto specialties. The best lunch strategy: graze stall to stall.

activities.name: Ninenzaka & Sannenzaka Streets
activities.description: Atmospheric stone-paved lanes lined with traditional shops — the most photogenic streets in all of Japan. Leads up toward Kiyomizu-dera area. The iconic five-story pagoda visible from the Higashiyama streets. Perfect photo background — you've seen it on every Japan Instagram.

activities.name: JR or Hankyu train back to Osaka
activities.description: ~30-45 minutes back to Osaka. Toddlers will probably sleep on the train — perfect.

days.title: Nara — Bowing Deer & Giant Buddha
days.description: A mellow day trip to ancient Nara — toddlers will go absolutely wild for the friendly deer. Visit the world's largest wooden building, then back to Osaka for a relaxed evening.

activities.name: Osaka → Nara (Kintetsu Railway)
activities.description: Take the Kintetsu-Nara line from Namba — ~35 minutes direct. Kintetsu-Nara station is closer to the park than JR Nara.

activities.name: Nara Park & Deer
activities.description: Over 1,200 wild but friendly deer roam freely. Buy shika senbei (deer crackers, ¥200) and watch the deer literally bow to you before eating. Toddlers + deer = pure magic (just watch for enthusiastic deer nudging small kids). Houses the world's largest bronze Buddha in the world's largest wooden building. The sheer scale leaves everyone speechless. Kids can try squeezing through the pillar hole (said to grant enlightenment).

activities.name: Return to Osaka
activities.description: Head back by mid-afternoon — toddlers will be deer-tired (pun intended). Train nap time.

activities.name: Shinsaibashi Shopping Street
activities.description: Osaka's main shopping arcade — covered, bright, and enormous. H&M, Uniqlo, Don Quijote, and tons of Japanese brands. Late-night shopping at its finest.

days.title: Osaka's Soul — Castles, Towers & Street Food
days.description: Explore Osaka's historic heart — the golden castle, the retro Shinsekai district, and Tsūtenkaku Tower. End with one last epic street food night in Namba.

activities.name: Osaka Castle (Ōsaka-jō)
activities.description: Toyotomi Hideyoshi's golden castle — one of Japan's most famous landmarks. The castle park is massive and toddler-friendly (huge open spaces). Inside the castle is a museum with elevator access.

activities.name: Shinsekai District
activities.description: Retro Osaka neighborhood frozen in time — neon signs, game arcades, and the iconic Tsūtenkaku Tower. It's like stepping into a 1960s Japanese movie set. Osaka's beloved retro tower — touch the Billiken statue's feet for good luck. Views of the entire city from the observation deck.

activities.name: Tennōji Park & Zoo
activities.description: If the toddlers need nature time, Tennōji Park has a nice garden (¥150), and Tennōji Zoo is right there. Simple, relaxed afternoon.

activities.name: Last Dōtonbori Night Walk
activities.description: One final stroll down the canal — catch anything you missed on Night 1. Pick up omiyage (souvenirs) for friends back home.

days.title: Sayonara Osaka — Last Bites & Flight Home
days.description: Pack up, grab a final matcha and some last-minute souvenirs, then head to Kansai International Airport. Until next time, Japan.

activities.name: Last-Minute Souvenir Shopping
activities.description: Hit Don Quijote or any depachika (department store basement food hall) for beautifully packaged Japanese sweets and snacks. Daimaru Shinsaibashi's basement is incredible.

activities.name: Osaka → Kansai International Airport (KIX)
activities.description: Take the Nankai Rapi:t limited express from Namba Station — direct to KIX in ~38 minutes. Futuristic train design — kids love it. Or the JR Haruka from Tennōji (~50 min).

activities.name: Kansai International Airport (KIX)
activities.description: Browse the duty-free shops for any final treats — Royce chocolate, matcha KitKats, and Japanese whisky. Last chance for konbini onigiri!
